core_obligations: Translate the statement into cohomology: Pic(X) = H^1(X, O_X^*) and Pic(Y) = H^1(Y, O_Y^*), and consider the Leray spectral sequence for O_X^* and f (proof lines 7953-7957).

Use the cited lemma on trivialization of invertible sheaves to see that the map H^1(X, O_X^*) -> H^0(Y, R^1f_*O_X^*) is zero, so that Leray gives H^1(X, O_X^*) = H^1(Y, f_*O_X^*) (proof lines 7958-7963).

Show the higher cohomology of any abelian sheaf on Y supported on the closed discrete subset T = Y setminus V vanishes, by combining the closed immersion and exactness results with the vanishing of H^i(T, F) for i > 0 (proof lines 7964-7976).

Break f^sharp : O_Y^* -> f_*O_X^* into the two short exact sequences through its kernel, image and cokernel, and use the vanishing to conclude successively that H^1(Y, O_Y^*) -> H^1(Y, Im f^sharp) and H^1(Y, Im f^sharp) -> H^1(Y, f_*O_X^*) are surjective, hence so is the pullback on Picard groups (proof lines 7977-7986).
proof_roadmap: Replace Picard groups by H^1 of the unit sheaf and set up Leray.
Kill the edge map so the Leray comparison becomes an equality.
Establish vanishing of higher cohomology for sheaves supported on the discrete complement.
Chain two surjectivity statements through the kernel-image-cokernel decomposition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a finite morphism f : X -> Y that is an isomorphism over an open V whose complement is discrete, the pullback map on Picard groups is surjective. The proof identifies Pic with H^1 of the unit sheaf, runs the Leray spectral sequence for O_X^*, observes that the edge map H^1(X, O_X^*) -> H^0(Y, R^1 f_*O_X^*) is zero by the cited divisor-trivialization lemma, so that H^1(X, O_X^*) = H^1(Y, f_*O_X^*), and then breaks O_Y^* -> f_*O_X^* into two short exact sequences whose kernel and cokernel are supported on the discrete complement, where higher cohomology vanishes (proof lines 7953-7986). H2: the two-step surjectivity argument through the Leray edge map and the vanishing on discrete supports is the substance.
